## Standard

<a id="NodePlatforms"></a>

### Node's platforms

`NodePlatforms` · `src/machine.ts:25`

The names Node gives to the system it runs on, as os.platform() answers: what a project lists among the systems it runs on.

Source: Node.js documentation: os.platform() · `https://nodejs.org/api/os.html#osplatform`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `aix` | `aix` | IBM AIX |
| `darwin` | `darwin` | macOS |
| `freebsd` | `freebsd` | FreeBSD |
| `linux` | `linux` | Linux |
| `openbsd` | `openbsd` | OpenBSD |
| `sunos` | `sunos` | Solaris |
| `win32` | `win32` | Windows |

- Maintained by: trame
- Serves: [The machine is asked once](product.md#AskedOnce)

## Message catalog

<a id="MachineWords"></a>

### What the questions say

`MachineWords` · `src/machine.ts:60`

<details><summary>The messages, in code</summary>

```typescript
() => ({
    systemSupported: (system: string) => `the system is one the project runs on: ${system}`,
    systemUnsupported: (system: string, systems: readonly string[]) => `the system is ${system}, which the project does not run on (${systems.join(", ")})`,
    nodeSupported: (version: string, least: number) => `Node ${version} is at least the major the project needs (${least})`,
    nodeTooOld: (version: string, least: number) => `Node ${version} is older than the major the project needs (${least})`,
    gitInstalled: () => "Git is installed",
    gitMissing: () => "Git does not answer: install it, the pull requests and the propagation need it",
  })
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Written in: [The language the questions speak in.](#MachineLanguage)
